nodes.title: Bernoulli Trials & Conditions
points: An experiment consists of repeated trials. A sequence of trials is called Bernoulli Trials if:
1. The number of trials 'n' is FINITE and fixed in advance.
2. Each trial has exactly TWO mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcomes: Success (S) and Failure (F).
3. The probability of success 'p' remains CONSTANT in every trial.
4. All trials are INDEPENDENT of each other.
Probability of failure: q = 1 − p ⟹ p + q = 1.

nodes.title: Binomial Random Variable & Notation
points: Let X denote the number of successes in n Bernoulli trials.
Then X is called a Binomial Random Variable, denoted: X ~ B(n, p).
Parameters of Binomial Distribution: Two parameters: n (number of trials) and p (probability of success).
Possible values taken by X: x ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3, ..., n} (total n + 1 possible values).

nodes.title: Probability Mass Function of B(n, p)
points: The PMF of X ~ B(n, p) is given by:
P(X = x) = p(x) = ⁿC_x · pˣ · q^(n − x), for x = 0, 1, 2, ..., n.
Combination formula: ⁿC_x = n! / [x! (n − x)!].
Total Probability Verification: ∑_(x=0)ⁿ P(X = x) = ∑ ⁿC_x pˣ q^(n−x) = (q + p)ⁿ = 1ⁿ = 1 (Binomial expansion).
Special Values: P(X = 0) = qⁿ; P(X = n) = pⁿ.

formulas.label: Binomial PMF
formulas.expr: P(X = x) = ⁿC_x pˣ q^(n − x)

nodes.title: Mean and Variance of Binomial Distribution
points: Expected Value (Mean): E[X] = μ = n p.
Variance: V(X) = σ² = n p q = n p (1 − p).
Standard Deviation: σ = √(n p q).
FUNDAMENTAL PROPERTY: For any Binomial Distribution, Variance is ALWAYS strictly LESS than Mean: V(X) < E[X] ⟹ n p q < n p (since q < 1).
If Variance ≥ Mean in any problem, it CANNOT be a binomial distribution!

formulas.label: Fundamental inequality
formulas.expr: Variance < Mean (n p q < n p)

nodes.title: 'At Least' and 'At Most' Probabilities
points: At Least k Successes: P(X ≥ k) = P(X = k) + P(X = k+1) + ... + P(X = n).
Master Shortcut for 'At Least 1 Success':
At Most k Successes: P(X ≤ k) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) + ... + P(X = k).
At Most 1 Success: P(X ≤ 1) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) = qⁿ + n p q^(n−1).

nodes.title: Maximum Variance of B(n, p)
points: Variance V(X) = n p (1 − p) = n(p − p²).
To maximize V(X), differentiate with respect to p: d/dp(p − p²) = 1 − 2p = 0 ⟹ p = ½.
Thus, for a given n, the variance is MAXIMUM when p = q = ½.
Maximum Variance Value: V_max = n(½)(½) = n / 4.
Example: For n = 16 trials, maximum possible variance is 16/4 = 4.

nodes.title: Recurrence Relation for Binomial Probabilities
points: Ratio of consecutive probabilities:
Recurrence Formula: P(X = x + 1) = [(n − x) / (x + 1)] · (p / q) · P(X = x).
Enables rapid step-by-step computation of the distribution table without recalculating large factorials.

nodes.title: Symmetry & Most Probable Value (Mode)
points: Symmetrical Distribution: When p = q = ½, the distribution is perfectly symmetrical about mean n/2.
Skewed Distribution: If p < ½, positively skewed (tail to right); if p > ½, negatively skewed (tail to left).
Mode (Most Probable Number of Successes):
Value of x for which P(X = x) is maximum.
If (n + 1)p is not an integer, mode is the integer part of (n + 1)p: Mode = ⌊(n + 1)p⌋.
If (n + 1)p is an integer m, the distribution is bimodal with modes at m − 1 and m.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Theorems & Problems
points: Board Favourite #1: A die is thrown 6 times. If 'getting an odd number' is a success, find probability of: (1) 5 successes, (2) at least 5 successes, (3) at most 5 successes.
Board Favourite #2: For a binomial distribution, Mean = 4 and Variance = 2. Find n, p, and P(X = 2).
Board Favourite #3: The probability that a bulb is defective is 0.1. In a sample of 5 bulbs, find probability that: (1) none is defective, (2) at least one is defective.
Board Favourite #4: How many times must a fair coin be tossed so that the probability of getting at least one head is more than 90%? (Use 1 − (½)ⁿ > 0.9 ⟹ (½)ⁿ < 0.1 ⟹ 2ⁿ > 10 ⟹ n ≥ 4).
Board Presentation Tip: Always write: 'Let X = number of successes, n = ..., p = ..., q = ..., X ~ B(n, p)'.

formulas.label: Find n and p
formulas.expr: q = V(X) / E[X] , p = 1 − q , n = E[X] / p

nodes.title: MHT-CET 10-Second Binomial Hacks & Traps
points: Parameter Extraction Hack: Given Mean μ and Variance σ²:
1. q = σ² / μ (instantly in 1 second!).
Example: Mean = 6, Variance = 2 ⟹ q = 2/6 = 1/3 ⟹ p = 2/3 ⟹ n = 6 / (2/3) = 9.
Impossibility Trap: Question: 'Can a binomial distribution have Mean = 6 and Variance = 8?' ⟹ Answer: NO! Variance must be less than Mean (npq < np).
Equal Probabilities Shortcut: If P(X = 1) = P(X = 2) for X ~ B(n, p): ⁿC₁ p q^(n−1) = ⁿC₂ p² q^(n−2) ⟹ n q = [n(n − 1)/2] p ⟹ 2q = (n − 1)p.
At Least 1 Success Shortcut: P(X ≥ 1) = 1 − qⁿ.
